_note: Applicability rules (Naya Beta, KNOW lane, 2026-10-11). Area codes are the 12 Team Naya areas. Keys are matched verbatim against entry topic/subtopic; keyword rules are lowercase substring matches over the entry's keyword haystack and are ADDITIVE to taxonomy rules. Thumb rule: subtopic > topic > keywords. 2026-11-17 taxonomy completion (Resolve, corpus-gate pass): topic rules added for the filing-era taxonomy (DESIGN/LESSON/VISION/DISTILLATION/LAW/DOCTRINE/TEAM/SMART_NOTE/LEARNING/VERIFICATION/WISDOM/ESSENCE/ONBOARDING/REPORT + spelling-variant mirrors), each derived from the entries' own declared topics. The generic SYSTEM topic is deliberately left unmapped: it is the filing loop's default bucket and carries no area signal — its entries stay needs_review for the KNOW/SN judgment-tagging pass rather than being blanket-tagged. 2026-11-18 judgment pass (Resolve, corpus judgment): the filing-era small-topic tail was judged topic by topic — rules added only where the topic's own meaning determines the area, each mirroring an existing canon mapping; SYSTEM-bucket entries with area-determinative subtopics were rescued by subtopic rules (16 entries); subtopic MISSION deliberately not ruled (shared with SN-0880, correctly HUMAN_VALUE via THE-VISION). Keys judged deliberately unmapped are recorded in standing_exclusions with reasons. needs_review at the pass tip: 362 -> 173 of 2,390 (7.2%), the residue being exactly the standing exclusions.

standing_exclusions._note: Deliberate standing exclusions (Resolve, corpus judgment pass, 2026-11-18). These keys are NOT unmapped by oversight: each was judged and left unmapped for the reason recorded, so the needs_review residue is an honest, judged number rather than an unexamined one. Revisit only when the recorded reason stops being true.

topics.SYSTEM: the filing loop's default bucket; the remainder carries no discriminating key (153 of 160 remaining entries have no subtopic at all and none carries a non-generic keyword). The 16 entries whose subtopics do determine an area were rescued by subtopic rules in this pass. Content-level tagging of the remainder is the manual-tag instrument's work (schema source='manual'), not the heuristic rule table's — ruling the bucket would be blanket-tagging, i.e. fabrication (2026-11-17 pass, reaffirmed).
topics.LIFECYCLE: the two entries (SN-9998, SN-9999) are provenance records for retired test fixtures. Tagging them into an area would present fixtures as usable knowledge and paper over the LAW lane's lifecycle-evidence class. They stay needs_review deliberately.
topics.NEWS: as filed, the topic carries no consistent area signal: one auto-titled stub (SN-2768) and one feed-creation note (SN-2789) whose honest home is the FEED rule — a filing-label correction for the SN lane, not a rule. A NEWS rule would mis-tag future news content as block design or as knowledge indifferently.
topics.JOURNEY: names a narrative form (a climb story), not an area. Single entry SN-2462.
topics.RHYTHM: names a cadence metaphor; the single entry (SN-2470) is a verdict-moment note. No area reads off the key.
topics.THE VERDICT: names a moment (a ruling received), not an area. Single entry SN-2490.
topics.THE FLOW: names a quality of experience, not an area; the single entry (SN-2488, a viewpoint design note) and its sibling FLOW entry belong to different areas, so no single rule can be honest for the key.
topics.FLOW: same defect as THE FLOW: the single entry (SN-2581, the creation flow) is product experience, its THE FLOW sibling is viewpoint design. The key names a quality, not an area.
topics.QUESTION: names an interrogative moment, not an area. Single entry SN-2577.
topics.SMART: a prefix fragment, not a topic; no area reads off it. Single entry SN-3182 (a design-philosophy note the SN lane may re-file under a real topic).
topics.FUTURE: names a time, not an area. The single entry (SN-3284, how children learn) is a learning note, but a FUTURE rule would mis-tag every future filing under the key.
topics.GO: a launch-moment label, not an area. Single entry SN-3293.

subtopics.MISSION: shared by SN-1879 + SN-1897 (topic SYSTEM, mission doctrine) and SN-0880 (topic THE-VISION, correctly tagged HUMAN_VALUE at 0.7 via its topic). A subtopic rule outranks the topic rule and would re-tag SN-0880 to LAW+KNOW — a side effect outside this pass. The two SYSTEM entries stay needs_review, named here, until a manual tag or a taxonomy split (e.g. a distinct mission-doctrine subtopic) separates them honestly.
subtopics.RESERVOIR: a metaphor (the reservoir of unfinished beginnings); the single entry SN-0805 is a state-of-the-system census. No area reads off the key.
subtopics.AI_WASTE: names a phenomenon, not a discipline; the single entry SN-0807 is a value-economics essay whose honest areas are a content judgment, not a key judgment.
subtopics.STANDARD: too generic to determine an area — any standard could belong to any lane. Single entry SN-0843.
subtopics.safety: a lowercase fragment of a safety taxonomy that does not yet exist; a single entry (SN-1882) does not build it. Left named rather than ruled from one sample.
subtopics.ownership: a lowercase fragment; the single entry (SN-1887) is a conduct-doctrine note whose area is a content judgment, not a key judgment.
